title: Input-position update rule
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state binary Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $w$ be a binary input, and fix $t,p\in\mathbb N$ with $p\le |w|+1$ and a finite list of bits $l$. Suppose the first bit of $l$ is false, its snapshot field decodes to the machine's snapshot on $w$ at time $t$, its boundary bits indicate whether $p=0$ and $p=|w|+1$, and its input-symbol bits encode the symbol read from $w$ at position $p$. Suppose its neighboring-head bits encode whether the input head at time $t$ is at $p-1$, at $p$, or at $p+1$ (with the left-neighbor condition also requiring $p\ge1$). Finally, suppose its designated chain bits encode the presence and value of the time-$(t+1)$ input-chain value at $p-1$, using no value when $p=0$. Then the local input-position update rule applied to $l$ yields the encoding of whether the input head at time $t+1$ is at $p$ and of the time-$(t+1)$ input-chain value at $p$.
